svg.metadata: {"asset_id":"garment-blues-class-b-shirt-male","name":"Men's Class B blue short-sleeve shirt and trousers (nametag position only)","size_in":{"w":26.8594,"h":29.5087},"units":"1 user unit = 0.01 in","viewBox":[0,0,2685.94,2950.87],"size_source":"estimated","size_basis":"Silhouette traced from images/base/blues_class_b_male.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px. Same canvas and scale assumption as the Class A coat. No real garment was measured. Then the whole sheet is scaled by 1.2171 (LIVE-ART2 item 1; 0.0474 in/px becomes 0.0577): the men's pocket measures 4.31 in wide on the traced image, and a USAF-style men's size-M short-sleeve shirt pocket is about 5.25 in wide x 6 in tall (ESTIMATE: AF shirt pattern dimension supplied with the task, no CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903 dimension; the CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.9 nametag (3 3/8 in) read as a ruler gives a smaller 4.56 in, the figure is schematic), so K = 5.25 / 4.313. The pocket is drawn 5.25 x 6.0 in, flap 2.02 in deep. Nameplate, epaulet strap width, buttons and strokes stay true g.title: Shirt epaulet strap, right shoulder: sewn into the armhole seam at the shoulder point, lying along the shoulder line, seen edge-on as a band 0.46 in thick (the strap is 1.0 in wide), pointed at the collar end, button 1/2 in from the tip, topstitched (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1 / 4.1.12.2, Figs 4.8, 4.10); the epaulet sleeve slides on over it

Shirt epaulet strap, left shoulder: sewn into the armhole seam at the shoulder point, lying along the shoulder line, seen edge-on as a band 0.46 in thick (the strap is 1.0 in wide), pointed at the collar end, button 1/2 in from the tip, topstitched (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1 / 4.1.12.2, Figs 4.8, 4.10); the epaulet sleeve slides on over it
Blue web belt (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1: blue belt with plain silver tip and buckle); flat strap with edge stitching

Open collar (top button undone, no tie): the shirt's fronts turned back from the roll lines, collar and revers, the inside of the collar band in the V, no wearer and no undershirt (the short sleeve's default; the tie is optional, CAPR 39-1 4.2.5.1.4, 4.2.6.3; 4.2.5.1.9, 4.2.6.9; Figs 4.16, 4.17). Draw above the body; collar insignia sit on the leaves

White V-neck undershirt seen in the open collar (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1 / 4.1.12.2: a V-neck or athletic style white undershirt is worn under the shirt): the front, the ribbed V neckband and the inside back; clipped to the open V, under the collar leaves; hidden with the open collar when the collar is closed

Blue tie, the Class A coat's tie: knot under the collar junction, blade straight down the placket, the tip over the belt buckle (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1.3, 4.1.8.3, Figs 4.6, 4.8); optional with short sleeves

Closed collar (top button buttoned, worn with the tie / tie tab): the back of the collar and the two leaves closing on the knot, as the long-sleeve sheet draws them; lies over the open collar and covers it (the short sleeve's second state; the tie is optional, CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1.3, 4.1.12.4)

rect.title: Nametag position (blank: cadet tags are blue, senior member tags silver) (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1.2.1.4)
